setup: Anchor a resistance band or strap to a sturdy point low in front of you, about level with your foot.
Sit on the floor or a mat facing the anchor with your working leg extended toward it.
Loop the free end over the top of the forefoot, across the instep and toes.
steps: Slide your hips back slowly to increase tension until the band draws the top of the foot and toes forward into plantarflexion.
Stop when you feel a mild to moderate stretch across the front of the ankle and shin.
Maintain the stretch steadily for the planned duration while keeping the lower leg relaxed.
Slowly ease tension off the band by moving toward the anchor, rest briefly, and switch sides.
instructions.breathing: Breathe slowly and rhythmically, exhaling to help the anterior shin muscles relax deeper into the stretch.
cues: Keep the calf and shin relaxed.
Stretch gently, do not force joint end-range.

common_faults.fault: Excessively inverting or twisting the foot while pulling.
common_faults.correction: Keep the line of pull straight so the foot points forward in a neutral sagittal plane.

common_faults.fault: Pulling aggressively to the point of impingement or sharp pain in the back of the ankle.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the band tension and aim only for a comfortable stretch across the anterior compartment.

precautions: Avoid forced end-range plantarflexion if you experience posterior ankle impingement or acute sprains.

name: Band Plantarflexion Stretch
summary: A seated mobility exercise using a band to gently pull the ankle into plantarflexion, stretching the tibialis anterior and anterior ankle structures.
